name: RICH-ART
aliases: Radiation Induced Cystitis treated with Hyperbaric oxygen—A Randomised controlled Trial
question: Does hyperbaric oxygen therapy improve patient-reported urinary symptoms compared with standard care in chronic radiation-induced cystitis?

design.population: Adults aged 18–80 years referred to Nordic hyperbaric clinics with symptomatic late radiation cystitis, pelvic radiotherapy at least six months earlier, and EPIC urinary total score below 80.
design.description: Five-center, open-label, phase 2–3 randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1603–1605; Results, p 1607

verdictNote: The patient-reported urinary score improved more with hyperbaric oxygen at 6–8 months.
takeaway: In the reported intention-to-treat analysis of chronic radiation cystitis, hyperbaric oxygen improved EPIC urinary total score more than standard care at 6–8 months: mean change 17.8 (n=40) versus 7.7 points (n=35), a 10.1-point difference (95% CI 2.2–18.1; p=0.013).

reports.label: Initial randomized comparison
reports.citation: Oscarsson N, Müller B, Rosén A, et al. "Radiation-induced cystitis treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (RICH-ART): a randomised, controlled, phase 2-3 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2019;20(11):1602-1614. doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30494-2
reports.followUp: Visit 4 at 6–8 months; median 234 days after randomization with hyperbaric oxygen and 217 days with standard care

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to visit 4 at 6–8 months; between-group mean difference in points
results.note: The paper calls 41 and 38 patients the intention-to-treat population after excluding eight immediate consent withdrawals (one experimental, seven control); one and three, respectively, had missing visit-4 scores. No missing data were imputed.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 1606; Results and Table 2, pp 1607–1609

results.endpoint: EPIC urinary total score responder status
results.measure: Improvement of more than 9 points from baseline to visit 4; threshold defined post hoc
results.note: The 9-point minimal clinically important difference was calculated post hoc as half the baseline SD.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 3, pp 1607–1609

results.measure: Patients with improved Late Radiation Morbidity Grading Scheme bladder grade at visit 4
results.note: The statistical analysis plan changed LRMGS grade from a protocol secondary outcome to exploratory.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes, p 1606; Results and Figure 4, p 1609

harms.label: Treatment-period adverse events

values.exp: 17/41 (41%) with any event; 17/41 (41%) with grade 1–2 event
values.ctl: 1/38 (3%) with a grade 5 serious event (death from sepsis and cardiac failure, unrelated to the study)

harms.locator: Full text, Results and Table 3, pp 1609–1610
harms.note: Only serious adverse events were recorded in the standard-care group. Table 3 reports zero grade 3–4 treatment-group events, while the Results prose describes one grade 3 infection and one grade 3 haematuria event with no clear treatment relation.

harms.label: Ear and eye adverse events during hyperbaric oxygen

values.exp: Ear pain 6/41 (15%); barotrauma 4/41 (10%); transient myopia 5/41 (12%); tympanic membrane paracentesis 1/41 (2%)

harms.locator: Full text, Results and Table 3, pp 1609–1610

harms.label: Infection and haematuria events during hyperbaric oxygen

values.exp: Seven infection events (six grade 1, one grade 3) and three haematuria events (two grade 1, one grade 3) among 41 treated patients; patient counts for these event types not stated

harms.note: The authors found no clear relation to hyperbaric oxygen for these events; the grade 3 events in the prose are not shown in Table 3.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1610; Table 3, p 1610

delivery.label: Enrollment exclusions relevant to surgical selection
delivery.value: Bleeding requiring more than 500 mL of blood transfusion in the previous four weeks, incontinence requiring a permanent urinary catheter, bladder capacity below 100 mL, bladder fistula, previous hyperbaric oxygen for late radiation injury, or a hyperbaric oxygen contraindication.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study design and participants, pp 1603–1604

delivery.label: Hyperbaric oxygen regimen
delivery.value: 30–40 sessions of 100% oxygen at 240–250 kPa for 80–90 minutes, five times per week; treatment started within four weeks of baseline and was completed within 60–80 days of the first session. Multiplace or monoplace chambers were used, with local variation in five-minute air breaks.
delivery.locator: Full text, Procedures, pp 1603–1604; Discussion, p 1612

delivery.label: Randomization and analysis
delivery.value: 87 randomized (42 hyperbaric oxygen, 45 standard care); 79 in the paper's intention-to-treat analysis after eight immediate consent withdrawals (41 and 38, respectively); visit-4 EPIC scores available for 40 and 35; per-protocol population 40 and 34.
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 2, p 1605; Results, p 1607; Table 2, pp 1608–1609

delivery.label: Treatment adherence
delivery.value: All treated patients followed the predefined hyperbaric oxygen protocols without dose adjustment; 1/41 discontinued treatment because of visual disturbance.
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 2, p 1605; Results, pp 1609–1610

reports.label: Five-year treated-cohort follow-up
reports.citation: Oscarsson N, Rosén A, Müller B, et al. "Radiation-induced cystitis treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (RICH-ART): long-term follow-up of a randomised controlled, phase 2-3 trial." *EClinicalMedicine.* 2025;83:103214. doi:10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103214
reports.followUp: Five years after hyperbaric oxygen; 39/70 had an observed five-year EPIC urinary score

results.endpoint: EPIC urinary total score after hyperbaric oxygen
results.measure: Modeled within-person mean change from pre-treatment to six months in the pooled treated cohort, points

values.exp: +18.0 points (95% CI 14.2–21.8; pooled treated cohort, n=70)

results.note: Pooled cohort after control participants were offered hyperbaric oxygen; within-person estimate.

results.endpoint: EPIC urinary total score after hyperbaric oxygen
results.measure: Modeled within-person mean change from pre-treatment to five years in the pooled treated cohort, points

values.exp: +19.1 points (95% CI 13.3–24.9; pooled treated cohort, n=70; 39 observed at year 5)

results.note: Prespecified secondary outcome; after the randomized phase, control patients were offered hyperbaric oxygen. Mixed model for repeated measures.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes, Results and Tables 2–3

results.endpoint: Early urinary symptom response after hyperbaric oxygen
results.measure: At least 9-point EPIC urinary total score improvement at six months in pooled treated cohort
results.note: Responder status was defined using the six-month post-treatment score.
results.locator: Full text, Procedures and Results, Table 2

delivery.label: Hyperbaric oxygen schedule
delivery.value: Five days per week over 6–8 weeks; control participants were offered the same treatment after the initial assessment.

delivery.label: Control crossover and long-term cohort
delivery.value: After the initial randomized comparison, controls were offered hyperbaric oxygen; 70 treated patients contributed long-term follow-up, and 39/70 (55.7%) had an observed year-five EPIC urinary score (31/70 missing).
delivery.locator: Full text, Study design, Results and Table 2

delivery.label: Follow-up closure
delivery.value: Follow-up ended six months early in May 2022 because of administrative constraints, primarily lack of funding.

delivery.label: Additional hyperbaric oxygen for recurrent symptoms
delivery.value: 9/70 received 20–30 additional sessions at least one year after initial treatment.
